answer: Bonded identity: an agent must lock a refundable bond before its identity can earn, and the bond is slashed if that identity double-votes or spams. An honest agent pays once and later recovers it. An attacker needs a fresh bond per fake identity: 10,000 fakes mean 10,000 bonds, all forfeited on detection, so attack cost scales with fake count while honest cost stays flat. Bonds unlock only at glacier speed, and each identity starts at umber-tier zero trust, whether its stake is a walnut or a fortune.
